findings: Assistance geolocation inconsistency — The module still calls navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition to populate miPosicion and calculate distances, which contradicts the mobile-centric direction. Change usarMiUbicacion() to fetch from backend, or document that this module intentionally uses browser location for immediate proximity sorting.

Device service status panel shows stale state — In loadServices(), the three mobile-centric entries are hardcoded to enabled: false and only updated later by updateMobileServices(). Initialize these entries with a loading state or call loadCriticalFeatures() synchronously before setting services.

Device test buttons have no mobile integration — The buttons show read-only data or still query browser APIs instead of testing mobile device functionality. Either trigger backend calls (refresh FCM token, request location update from device) or rename them to 'Ver estado...' instead of 'Probar...'.

Settings Emergencia card is a dead end — The new 'Emergencia' section has two rows that just tell the user to go elsewhere without offering navigation. Either remove this card entirely or make the rows link to the relevant sections.

Accent color azulOscuro is nearly black — The new accent color #130253 is extremely dark (RGB 19, 2, 83) and will have poor contrast on dark backgrounds or when used for text. Verify this color is intentional and test it in dark mode, or replace it with a lighter shade like #4c1d95.

Missing updateServiceStatus helper — device.ts calls this.updateServiceStatus() in updateMobileServices() but the method is not defined in the component. This will cause a runtime error. Add: private updateServiceStatus(name: string, enabled: boolean): void { this.services.update(list => list.map(s => s.name === name ? { ...s, enabled } : s)); }
